moments.name: Electric battery
moments.description: Alessandro Volta described the voltaic pile, the first battery to give a steady electric current, in a letter to the Royal Society.

moments.name: Electromagnetic induction
moments.description: Michael Faraday showed that a changing magnetic field produces an electric current, the principle behind generators, transformers and microphones.

moments.name: Telephone
moments.description: Alexander Graham Bell was granted a patent for the telephone, which carries speech as an electric current.

moments.name: Transistor
moments.description: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain, working with William Shockley at Bell Labs, made the first working transistor, a point-contact transistor.
moments.location: Murray Hill, New Jersey, United States

moments.name: Integrated circuit
moments.description: Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments demonstrated the first integrated circuit, with several components on a single piece of semiconductor.

moments.name: Capacitive touchscreen
moments.description: E. A. Johnson at the Royal Radar Establishment described a touchscreen that senses a finger by the change in capacitance.

moments.name: Liquid-crystal display
moments.description: George Heilmeier's team at RCA demonstrated the first liquid-crystal displays.

moments.name: ARPANET
moments.description: The first message was sent over ARPANET, from UCLA to the Stanford Research Institute. ARPANET grew into the internet.

moments.name: Microprocessor
moments.description: Intel introduced the 4004, the first commercial microprocessor: a whole computer processor on one chip.

moments.name: Mobile phone
moments.description: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first public call from a handheld mobile phone.

moments.name: World Wide Web
moments.description: Tim Berners-Lee wrote the proposal for the World Wide Web at CERN.

moments.name: Lithium-ion battery
moments.description: Sony sold the first commercial lithium-ion battery: light, rechargeable and able to hold a lot of energy.

moments.name: iPhone
moments.description: Steve Jobs announced the iPhone, a phone controlled by a multi-touch screen, with the web in your pocket.

moments.name: Truman Doctrine
moments.description: President Harry S. Truman pledged to support countries resisting Soviet pressure. It is often taken as the start of the Cold War.

moments.name: Sputnik 1
moments.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, starting the Space Race.

moments.name: Apollo 11 Moon landing
moments.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon. The Apollo Guidance Computer that helped get them there was built from integrated circuits.

moments.name: Apollo-Soyuz Test Project
moments.description: An American Apollo spacecraft and a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit. It is usually taken as the end of the Space Race.

moments.name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
moments.description: East Germany opened the border crossings in the Berlin Wall, and crowds began to tear it down.

moments.name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
moments.description: The Soviet Union was formally dissolved, ending the Cold War.

moments.name: Start of the Information Age
moments.description: The Information Age is usually said to have begun in the 1970s, as computers and digital communication spread. Historians don't agree on an exact date.

periods.name: Cold War
periods.description: A long rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union and their allies, without direct war between the two.

periods.name: Space Race
periods.description: The competition between the Soviet Union and the United States to be first to achieve milestones in spaceflight.

periods.name: Information Age
periods.description: The period in which computers and digital communication have shaped how people work, learn and live. It is still going on.
